questions: With 16 mm footprints at 12 mm spacing, does the signal stay monotonic across the 25 mm tape, or do the outer sensors saturate early and reduce steering authority?
Did moving the sensors back to y = 0.05 m reduce overshoot on the s-bend and slalom compared with the baseline, or did the lag change make oscillation worse?
Does the lower mass (0.5 kg) and smaller wheel radius (0.03 m) reach speeds that the controller can use, or do the wheels saturate and slip on the bends?
Which tracks still end off track, and at what progress? Is the failure point the same on each track?
What single geometry parameter would you change next to lower max_error?

intent: Widen the sensor capture range (16 mm footprints at 12 mm spacing across a 48 mm array), move the sensors slightly back to y = 0.05 m to reduce steering lag, and lower mass and wheel radius to increase acceleration and turn authority. The goal is to move the best measured progress from 0.155 toward finishing the course, with fewer line-loss events and lower max_error. Body width is kept at 0.12 m because it has no effect below 0.18 m (the 0.06 m floor governs the off-track limit).
learning: Baseline evidence: uniform off-track failures at progress 0.10 to 0.16, max_error 0.062 to 0.069 m, and 1 to 2 line-loss events per run. Body width has no effect below 0.18 m because the 0.06 m floor governs the off-track limit. Hypotheses for this iteration: (H1) 16 mm footprints at 12 mm spacing reduce line-loss events. (H2) Sensors at y = 0.05 m reduce overshoot compared with 0.04 m. (H3) Mass 0.5 kg and wheel radius 0.03 m raise the achieved speed without slip. Check H1 through line_loss_events, H2 through steering_oscillation, and H3 through progress and completion_time.
rationale:
The development evidence (entityR2A) is uniform. All 60 trials ended off track, with progress only 0.105 to 0.155 and no finishes. Mean max_error is 0.062 to 0.069 m, just past the off-track limit. The rms_error (about 0.028 m) is similar on every track, so the drift is not a single-track problem. Line loss happened once or twice per run, which points at the robot leaving the tape on the first bend rather than oscillating for long. Steering oscillation is modest (0.07 to 0.15).

Body width cannot help. The limit is max(0.06, 0.0125 + body_width/4), and the largest allowed body_width of 0.18 m gives 0.0575, so the 0.06 m floor stays in force across the whole range. Body length has no dynamic effect. So the geometry levers left are the sensor array and the drive dynamics.

Changes made, with reasons:
1. Sensor footprint 12 mm to 16 mm. A larger footprint covers more of the 25 mm tape at once, which smooths the signal and reduces the sudden dropouts that cause line loss.
2. Sensor spacing 10 mm to 12 mm, at x = +0.024, +0.012, 0, -0.012, -0.024. The array spans 48 mm, so at least one or two sensors stay on the tape when the robot drifts by up to about 0.03 m. This widens the capture range that the prior design lacked.
3. Sensors moved slightly back to y = 0.05 m. This reduces the lead between sensing and steering, which should cut overshoot on the s-bend and slalom. The 0.04 m offset was an untested guess.
4. Mass 0.6 kg to 0.5 kg and wheel radius 0.035 m to 0.03 m. Lower inertia helps the robot reach the roughly 1.5 m/s average speed needed to finish in 3 s. The smaller wheel gives more turn authority per unit of wheel command, which helps the tighter bends.
5. Wheel track kept at 0.12 m and body width at 0.12 m (no effect on the limit, kept as a neutral value). Sensor weights kept at [2, 1, 0, -1, -2] so the sign convention is unchanged.

Expected result: fewer line-loss events and a larger off-track margin on the development tracks. The robot should get further along each track (progress above 0.3 is the first milestone), and the Integrator should be able to tune gains against a steadier signal.
